title: What is Bitcoin?
script: Bitcoin is digital money with no bank, no government, no middleman. It runs on a network of computers that verify every transaction. Only 21 million will ever exist. That fixed supply is why people call it digital gold.

title: What is Blockchain?
script: A blockchain is a public ledger copied across thousands of computers. Every new transaction gets bundled into a block, linked to the last one, and locked with cryptography. Once it's in, it can't be changed. That's what makes it trustworthy.

title: Bitcoin Halving Explained
script: Every 4 years, Bitcoin miner rewards get cut in half. Less new supply enters the market while demand stays the same. Historically, halvings have preceded major bull markets. Supply shock, meet demand.

title: Hot Wallet vs Cold Wallet
script: Hot wallets stay connected to the internet — convenient but riskier. Cold wallets stay offline — safer for long-term holding. Rule of thumb: spending money hot, savings cold. Never share your seed phrase.

title: What is a Seed Phrase?
script: Your seed phrase is 12 to 24 words that control your entire wallet. Anyone with these words owns your funds. Write it on paper, never a screenshot. Lose it, and there's no customer support to call.

title: Custodial vs Non-Custodial Wallets
script: Custodial wallets — like exchanges — hold your keys for you. Non-custodial wallets put you in full control. 'Not your keys, not your coins' exists for a reason. Convenience comes with trust, control comes with responsibility.

title: What is Market Cap?
script: Market cap equals price times circulating supply. A low price doesn't mean a coin is cheap — a $1 coin with 100 billion supply can have a bigger market cap than a $60,000 coin with 19 million supply.

title: What is Liquidity?
script: Liquidity is how easily you can buy or sell without moving the price. High liquidity means tight spreads and smooth trades. Low liquidity means one big order can swing the price 20%. Always check volume before trading.

title: What is a Stop Loss?
script: A stop loss automatically sells your position if price drops to a set level. It caps your downside without you watching charts all day. No stop loss means no plan for when you're wrong.

title: Spot vs Futures Trading
script: Spot trading means you own the actual asset. Futures let you trade with leverage without owning anything, multiplying both gains and losses. Beginners: spot first. Leverage forgives nothing.

title: What is Volatility?
script: Volatility measures how fast and far price swings. Crypto moves 5-10% in a day where stocks move 1%. Higher volatility means higher risk and higher potential reward. Size your positions accordingly.

title: What is DeFi?
script: DeFi means decentralized finance — lending, borrowing, and trading without banks. Smart contracts replace the middleman. Anyone with a wallet and internet can access it. No credit check, no approval process.

title: What is a Liquidity Pool?
script: A liquidity pool is a shared pot of two tokens that lets people trade without a traditional order book. Providers deposit funds and earn fees. But watch out for impermanent loss when prices diverge.

title: What is Yield Farming?
script: Yield farming means moving crypto between protocols to earn the highest returns. High yields often mean high risk — smart contract bugs, rug pulls, or token crashes. If the APY looks insane, ask why.

title: What is a Smart Contract?
script: A smart contract is code that executes automatically when conditions are met. No lawyer, no middleman, no trust required — just code. It powers everything from lending to NFTs to DAOs.

title: What is an NFT?
script: An NFT is a unique digital certificate of ownership stored on a blockchain. Unlike Bitcoin, each one is one-of-a-kind — not interchangeable. It can represent art, tickets, game items, or real-world assets.

title: What is a Stablecoin?
script: Stablecoins are pegged to a stable asset like the US dollar, staying near $1. They're used to move value fast without volatility risk. USDT and USDC are the two biggest by far.

title: Token vs Coin
script: A coin has its own blockchain — like Bitcoin or Ethereum. A token is built on top of an existing blockchain, like an ERC-20 token on Ethereum. Different infrastructure, different trust assumptions.

title: What is Tokenomics?
script: Tokenomics is the economic design of a crypto asset — total supply, distribution, inflation rate, and utility. Bad tokenomics can crash even a great project. Always check supply schedule before you buy.

title: Proof of Work vs Proof of Stake
script: Proof of Work uses computing power to validate transactions — that's Bitcoin. Proof of Stake uses staked coins instead — that's Ethereum since 2022. PoS uses over 99% less energy.

title: What is Crypto Mining?
script: Mining is solving complex math puzzles to validate transactions and earn new coins. It secures the network and requires massive computing power. As difficulty rises, mining gets harder and more competitive.

title: What is Staking?
script: Staking means locking up your coins to help secure a Proof of Stake network. In return, you earn rewards — like interest for participating. Higher risk than a savings account, but no mining rig required.

title: What is a Rug Pull?
script: A rug pull happens when developers drain liquidity or dump tokens, crashing the price to zero. Red flags: anonymous team, no audit, and locked liquidity that isn't actually locked. Do your research before you buy.

title: How to Spot a Crypto Scam
script: Guaranteed returns, urgency to act now, and DMs from 'support' are massive red flags. No legitimate project asks for your seed phrase. If it sounds too good to be true, it always is.

title: What is a 51% Attack?
script: A 51% attack happens when one entity controls over half a network's mining or staking power, letting them rewrite transactions. Bigger networks like Bitcoin are nearly impossible to attack this way — smaller chains are more vulnerable.

title: What is a Crypto ETF?
script: A crypto ETF lets investors get exposure to Bitcoin or Ethereum through a regular brokerage account — no wallet needed. It opened the door for institutional and retail investors who wouldn't otherwise touch crypto directly.

title: Why Does the Fed Affect Crypto?
script: When interest rates rise, investors move money into safer assets, pulling liquidity out of risk assets like crypto. When rates fall, cheap money flows back in. Crypto often moves with — not against — broader markets.

title: What Drives Bitcoin's Price?
script: Bitcoin's price moves on supply and demand, institutional adoption, regulation news, and macro liquidity. No single factor controls it. The best traders watch all of them together, not one headline at a time.

title: What is Ethereum?
script: Ethereum isn't just money — it's a programmable blockchain. Developers build apps, tokens, and entire financial systems on top of it. If Bitcoin is digital gold, Ethereum is a digital economy.

title: What is a Fork?
script: A fork happens when a blockchain splits into two paths, usually over a disagreement on rules. A hard fork creates an entirely new chain. Bitcoin Cash splitting from Bitcoin in 2017 is a famous example.

title: What is an Order Book?
script: An order book shows every buy and sell order waiting to be filled at each price. Reading it shows you where big buyers and sellers are sitting — useful for spotting support and resistance.

title: Support and Resistance Explained
script: Support is a price level where buying pressure tends to stop a drop. Resistance is where selling pressure tends to stop a rally. Prices often bounce between these levels before breaking through.

title: What is DCA?
script: DCA means buying a fixed amount at regular intervals, regardless of price. It smooths out volatility and removes the pressure to time the market perfectly. Simple, boring, and historically effective.

title: What is RSI?
script: RSI measures whether an asset is overbought or oversold on a scale of 0 to 100. Above 70 often signals overbought, below 30 oversold. It's a signal, not a guarantee — always confirm with other data.

title: What is a DAO?
script: A DAO is an organization run by code and community votes instead of a CEO. Token holders propose and vote on decisions, from treasury spending to protocol upgrades. Governance, decentralized.

title: What is Impermanent Loss?
script: Impermanent loss happens when the price of tokens in a liquidity pool diverges after you deposit them. The bigger the price gap, the bigger the loss compared to just holding. It's the hidden cost of providing liquidity.

title: What are Gas Fees?
script: Gas fees are the cost of processing a transaction on a blockchain like Ethereum. They rise when the network is congested and fall when it's quiet. Layer 2 networks exist specifically to cut these costs.

title: What is a Layer 2?
script: Layer 2 networks process transactions off the main blockchain, then settle back to it in batches. Result: faster speeds, lower fees, same underlying security. Arbitrum and Base are two popular examples.

title: What is a Whitepaper?
script: A whitepaper is a project's founding document — explaining the problem, the solution, and the technology. Before you invest in any token, read the whitepaper. If there isn't one, that's your answer.

title: What is Circulating Supply?
script: Circulating supply is the number of coins currently available in the market — not locked, not vested, not held by the team. It's what actually drives market cap and price impact from trading.

title: What is a Smart Contract Audit?
script: An audit is an independent review of a project's code, looking for bugs and vulnerabilities before hackers do. No audit doesn't always mean scam, but it does mean higher unverified risk.

title: What is a Phishing Attack in Crypto?
script: Phishing scams trick you into entering your seed phrase or private key on a fake site. Fake wallet pop-ups, fake airdrops, and fake support DMs are the most common bait. Always verify the URL.

title: What is Regulatory Risk?
script: Regulatory risk is the chance that new laws restrict how crypto can be used, traded, or taxed. Different countries take very different approaches — from full bans to full adoption. Rules can shift fast.

title: What is Institutional Adoption?
script: Institutional adoption means banks, funds, and corporations holding or offering crypto products. It brings liquidity and legitimacy — but also more correlation with traditional markets during downturns.

title: What is a Bull vs Bear Market?
script: A bull market means sustained rising prices and optimism. A bear market means sustained falling prices and fear. Both are normal cycles — the goal is having a plan for each, not predicting when they'll flip.

title: What is Leverage?
script: Leverage lets you trade with borrowed funds, amplifying both gains and losses. 10x leverage means a 10% move against you wipes out your entire position. It's a tool for the experienced, not the curious.

title: What is a Limit Order vs Market Order?
script: A market order fills instantly at the current price. A limit order only fills at the price you set, or better. Market orders guarantee speed, limit orders guarantee price. You rarely get both.

title: What is a Bridge?
script: A bridge lets you move assets between different blockchains that otherwise can't talk to each other. Convenient, but bridges are one of the most hacked parts of crypto infrastructure — use established ones only.

title: What is Total Value Locked (TVL)?
script: TVL is the total amount of crypto deposited in a DeFi protocol. Higher TVL generally signals more trust and adoption. It's one of the fastest ways to gauge a protocol's real usage.

title: What is an Airdrop?
script: An airdrop is free tokens distributed to a project's early users or community, often to reward loyalty or bootstrap adoption. Great when legitimate — but never pay gas fees to 'claim' a suspicious one.

title: What is Vesting?
script: Vesting locks team and investor tokens for a set period before they can be sold. It prevents early dumps that crash the price. Always check the vesting schedule before a token unlock date.

title: What is a Public and Private Key?
script: Your public key is like your bank account number — safe to share. Your private key is like your PIN — never share it. Whoever holds the private key controls the funds. Period.

title: What is a Block Explorer?
script: A block explorer lets you view every transaction on a blockchain in real time — wallet balances, transfer history, contract activity. It's completely public. Nothing on-chain is truly private.

title: What is Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) for Crypto?
script: 2FA adds a second verification step beyond your password, usually a code from an app. Use an authenticator app, not SMS — SIM swap attacks specifically target text-message 2FA on exchange accounts.

title: What is a Hardware Wallet?
script: A hardware wallet stores your private keys on a physical device, completely offline. Even if your computer is hacked, your keys never touch the internet. The gold standard for serious cold storage.

title: What is Quantitative Tightening and Why Crypto Cares?
script: Quantitative tightening is when central banks pull money out of the financial system, reducing overall liquidity. Less liquidity generally means less capital flowing into risk assets like crypto. Watch the macro, not just the charts.

title: What is the Correlation Between Bitcoin and Stocks?
script: Bitcoin used to trade independently of stocks. Since institutional adoption grew, it now often moves with the Nasdaq during macro events. Correlation isn't fixed — it shifts based on who's holding the asset.

title: What is Slippage?
script: Slippage is the difference between your expected trade price and the actual price you get filled at. It's worse in low-liquidity markets or during high volatility. Always check the slippage tolerance before you swap.

title: What is FOMO in Crypto?
script: FOMO — fear of missing out — drives people to buy at the top after a huge rally, chasing gains that already happened. It's an emotional trap, not a strategy. The best trades are boring, not thrilling.

title: What is a Consensus Mechanism?
script: A consensus mechanism is how a decentralized network agrees on which transactions are valid — without a central authority. Proof of Work and Proof of Stake are the two most common. No consensus, no trust.
